name: Arba'a Turub
description: Arba'a Turub (literally Four Packs of Cards) is a massive-scale Somali partnership game that pushes the boundaries of traditional trick-taking. Using a staggering 144-card deck and hands of 36 cards each, it combines the structural logic of Whist with an unusual 'Progressive Win' condition that requires a team to outdo their own previous performance to claim the match.

content.text: Arba'a Turub (literally Four Packs of Cards) is a massive-scale Somali partnership game that pushes the boundaries of traditional trick-taking. Using a staggering 144-card deck and hands of 36 cards each, it combines the structural logic of Whist with an unusual 'Progressive Win' condition that requires a team to outdo their own previous performance to claim the match.

A unique Somali evolution of European Whist, likely developed during periods of colonial influence and adapted to local social settings. Its name 'Arba'a Turub' signifies the four decks required to play.
4 players in two fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
144 cards. Prepared by taking four 52-card decks and removing all 2s, 3s, 4s, and 5s. Ranks: A(high), K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6(low).
Four identical decks, table space large enough for 144 cards.

Deal starts clockwise. Each player receives 36 cards in batches of 3. **Crucial**: After the first 3 cards are dealt to the player on the dealer's left (Eldest Hand), they must declare trumps immediately.

items.text: Two-Pack Variant: A faster version using only 72 cards (two decks).
